claims.harm: plumbing logger instances through kernel objects makes the logging interface cumbersome and easy to misuse if forgetting to log to context cannot be enforced
claims.quote: logging interface becomes more cumbersome, i.e. caller has to figure out if a logger is in scope and if it should be used. It is easy to misuse (e.g. forget to log to context when it exists, which seems hard to enforce.)

status_by.quote: Nice, I hadn't thought of a per-file approach, that seems elegant.

status_by.quote: I just don't think it's currently important as it seems users (incl myself) don't actually need this. Just making kernel logging explicitly global... seems like the more pragmatic change to me now.
